instruction: Find the FAQ area related to accessible seating and ticket availability.

metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to the accessible seating FAQ page on premier.ticketek.com.au. The evaluator checks if the active tab URL contains both 'Accessible' and 'FAQ' patterns using regex matching. This is a similar navigation task to the original but targets a different FAQ section.
metadata.verification: Uses existing is_expected_url_pattern_match metric with active_tab_info getter. The expected patterns 'Accessible' and 'FAQ' should match URLs like '/help/FAQs/Accessible-Seating' or similar variations on the Ticketek website.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_active_tab_info can extract the active tab URL from accessibility tree and return it as a dict with 'url' field
Metric logic is correct: is_expected_url_pattern_match properly handles both string URLs and dict inputs, uses re.search to check all patterns exist in URL
Coverage is complete: Checks for both 'Accessible' and 'FAQ' in URL, which semantically verifies the instruction requirement to navigate to accessible seating FAQ section
Pattern case-sensitivity issue: Patterns 'Accessible' and 'FAQ' are case-sensitive, may fail if URL uses lowercase 'accessible', 'faq' or mixed case variations
Pattern specificity could be improved: Simple substring patterns might match unintended pages or miss valid variations (e.g., 'accessibility' vs 'Accessible', 'FAQs' vs 'FAQ')
No postconfig needed: URL verification doesn't depend on UI state, so evaluator will work correctly at runtime
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider making patterns case-insensitive by using re.IGNORECASE flag or converting URL to lowercase before matching
Consider using more specific regex patterns like '(?i)accessible.*seating' and '(?i)faq' to better match the intended page and reduce false positives
Consider adding pattern for 'ticketek.com.au' domain to ensure navigation stayed on the correct website
